He played [[college basketball]] for the [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU Tigers]], and was drafted in the second round of the [[2019 NBA draft]] by the [[Boston Celtics]]. ==Early life== Waters played at [[South Kent School]], a private all-boys school in Connecticut for three years. He transferred prior to his senior year to [[Notre Dame High School (West Haven, Connecticut)|Notre Dame High School]] in [[West Haven, Connecticut]]. In 2015, he tried out for the [[Puerto Rico men's national basketball team]]'s U-17 squad.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nhregister.com/colleges/article/Tremont-Waters-looking-to-earn-spot-on-Team-11353716.php|title = Tremont Waters looking to earn spot on Team Puerto Rico|date = March 25, 2015}} One of the wishes of his late father was for him to come to [[Puerto Rico]] and explore his [[Puerto Ricans|Puerto Rican]] roots on his mother's side, since his mother Vanessa has family in [[San Juan, Puerto Rico|San Juan]]. As a senior, he was selected for the [[Jordan Brand Classic]]. He initially committed to [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]] but decommitted shortly before coach [[John Thompson III]] was fired.{{cite news |last1=Halley |first1=Jim |title=Jordan Brand Classic: Tremont Waters testing the recruiting waters again |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/jordan-brand-classic-player-tremont-waters-is-testing-the-recruiting-waters-again |access-date=July 17, 2018 |work=[[USA Today]] |date=April 13, 2017}} Ranked number 37 overall in his high school class by [[Rivals.com]], Waters committed to [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU]] and coach [[Will Wade (basketball)|Will Wade]] on June 5, 2017.{{cite news |last1=Payne |first1=Terrence |title=Tremont Waters commits to LSU |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2017/06/05/tremont-waters-commits-to-lsu/ |access-date=July 17, 2018 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=June 5, 2017}} Waters was the 2017 Gatorade and Register State Player of the Year in Connecticut.{{cite news |last1=Borges |first1=David |title=New Haven's Tremont Waters working to get better on and off the court |url=https://www.nhregister.com/sports/article/New-Haven-s-Tremont-Waters-working-to-get-12923680.php |access-date=July 18, 2018 |work=[[New Haven Register]] |date=May 17, 2018}} ==College career== On November 22, 2017, Waters scored a season-high 39 points on 13-of-22 shooting in a 94–84 loss to [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]].{{cite news |title=Marquette beats LSU 94-84 for third in Maui |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401000098 |access-date=July 17, 2018 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 22, 2017}} As a freshman at LSU, Waters averaged 15.9 points, 6.0 assists and 3.4 rebounds per game. His 198 assists broke the school record for assists by a freshman set by [[Ben Simmons]]. Waters was named to the Freshman All-SEC team and was the Freshman of the Year in Louisiana. After the season, Waters entered his name in the [[2018 NBA draft]] but did not hire an agent to preserve his collegiate eligibility.{{cite news |last1=Lopez |first1=Andrew |title=LSU freshman guard Tremont Waters enters name for NBA Draft |url=https://www.nola.com/lsu/index.ssf/2018/04/lsu_freshman_guard_tremont_wat.html |access-date=July 17, 2018 |work=[[The Times-Picayune]] |date=April 24, 2018}} He announced his return to LSU for his sophomore season on May 29, 2018.{{cite news |last1=Miller |first1=Brody |title=Tremont Waters returning to LSU for sophomore season |url=https://www.nola.com/lsu/index.ssf/2018/05/tremont_waters_returning_to_ls.html |access-date=July 18, 2018 |work=[[The Times-Picayune]] |date=May 30, 2018}} Waters scored the game-winning layup for LSU against the No. 6 seeded [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland Terrapins]] in the second round of the 2019 NCAA tournament on March 23, 2019.{{Cite magazine|last=Staples|first=Andy|title=Like it or not, LSU finds a way to keep dancing|url=https://www.si.com/college/2019/03/23/lsu-maryland-tremont-waters-march-madness-will-wade|access-date=August 2, 2020|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=March 23, 2019 |language=en-us}} Waters shot 39.6 percent (17 of 43) from the field in the tournament, averaging 16.7 points, 4.7 assists and 1.7 steals per game.{{Cite web|title=Tremont Waters - 2018-19 - Men's Basketball|url=https://lsusports.net/sports/mens-basketball/roster/tremont-waters/5352|access-date=August 3, 2020|website=LSU Tigers|date=July 8, 2019|language=en}} He earned All-SEC first team honors that season along with his strong tournament performance.{{Cite web|title=2019 SEC Men's Basketball Awards announced|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/26238088/2019-sec-men-basketball-awards-announced|access-date=July 30, 2020|website=www.secsports.com}} ==Professional career== ===Boston Celtics (2019–2021)=== On June 20, 2019, Waters was selected with the 51st overall pick in the [[2019 NBA draft]] by the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|title=2019 NBA Draft results: Picks 1-60|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2019/06/21/2019-nba-draft-results-picks-1-60|website=NBA.com|date=June 21, 2019|access-date=June 21, 2019}} Waters played for the Celtics during the 2019 [[NBA Summer League]] season and averaged 10.0 points, 5.3 assists, 2.0 rebounds, and 2.0 steals in 22.5 minutes through the first four games helping the Celtics clinch the number one seed going into the tournament.{{cite web|title=Tremont Waters Player Profile|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Tremont-Waters/Summary/88918|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 23, 2021}} On July 12, 2019, Waters' father was found dead at a Super 8 Hotel room in [[West Haven, Connecticut]] in an apparent suicide.{{cite web|title=Dad of Celtics draft pick Tremont Waters found dead in Connecticut hotel room|url=https://nypost.com/2019/07/12/father-of-celtics-draft-pick-tremont-waters-found-dead-in-connecticut-hotel/|website=NYPost.com|date=July 12, 2019|access-date=July 12, 2019}} Despite this, Waters played 32 minutes in the tournament game the following day, July 13. The Celtics fell short to the [[Memphis Grizzlies|Grizzlies]] and were eliminated from Summer League Championship contention despite a 16-point effort from Waters.{{cite web|title=Grizzlies vs Celtics - Box Score|url=https://www.espn.com/nba-summer-league/boxscore?gameId=401144606&league=nba-summer-las-vegas|website=ESPN.com|date=July 13, 2019|access-date=December 23, 2021}} Waters concluded his 2019 Summer League run leading the team in minutes per game as well as averaging 11.2 points, a team high 4.8 assists, and 2.0 steals. On July 25, 2019, the Celtics announced that they had signed Waters to a [[two-way contract]], splitting time with the [[Maine Celtics|Maine Red Claws]].{{cite web|title=Celtics Sign Four Players Max Strus, Tremont Waters sign Boston's two-way contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-four-players|work=NBA.com|date=July 25, 2019|access-date=July 25, 2019}} He scored 24 points in two games in the [[NBA G League]] in November. On November 24, the Celtics recalled Waters after an injury to [[Kemba Walker]].{{cite news|first=Cody|last=Taylor|title=Celtics recall Tremont Waters from the G League for the first time|url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2019/11/24/boston-celtics-recall-tremont-waters-g-league-maine-red-claws/|work=Rookie Wire|date=November 24, 2019|access-date=November 25, 2019}} On January 9, 2020, Waters posted 30 points, seven assists and five steals for Maine in a 120-118 triple overtime win over the [[Capital City Go-Go]].{{cite news|title=Sports Digest: Red Claws outlast Go-Go in three overtimes, 120-118|url=https://www.pressherald.com/2020/01/09/sports-digest-red-claws-outlast-go-go-in-three-overtimes-120-118/|work=[[Portland Press Herald]]|date=January 9, 2020|access-date=June 22, 2020}} He averaged 18.0 points, 7.3 assists, 3.2 rebounds and 1.89 steals per game in 36 G League games. On June 18, 2020, Waters was named [[NBA G League Rookie of the Year Award|NBA G League Rookie of the Year]].{{cite web|title=Maine Red Claws' Tremont Waters Named 2019-20 NBA G League Rookie Of The Year|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/maine-red-claws-tremont-waters-named-2019-20-nba-g-league-rookie-of-the-year/|website=NBA.com|date=June 18, 2020|access-date=June 18, 2020}} On November 23, 2020, Waters re-signed with the Celtics.{{cite web|title=NBA Player transactions|url=https://www.nba.com/stats/transactions/|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 23, 2020}} ===Wisconsin Herd (2021)=== On Frank Mason in a trade|url=https://fox11online.com/sports/bucks-and-nba/herd-acquire-frank-mason-in-a-trade|work=Fox 11 News|date=February 24, 2022|access-date=February 26, 2022}} ===South Bay Lakers (2022)=== On February 24, 2022, Waters was traded, along with a 2022 second-round pick, to the [[South Bay Lakers]] in exchange for [[Frank Mason III]] and a 2022 first-round pick. ===Gigantes de Carolina (2022–2023)=== On March 1, 2022, Waters was selected with the first pick overall in the 2022 [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] draft by the [[Gigantes de Carolina (men's basketball)|Gigantes de Carolina]]{{cite web |last=Figueroa Loza |first=Jorge |date=March 1, 2022 |title=Comprometido Tremont Waters para jugar con los Gigantes en el BSN: "Ya tenemos un acuerdo con él" |url=https://www.elnuevodia.com/deportes/baloncesto/notas/comprometido-tremont-waters-para-jugar-con-los-gigantes-en-el-bsn-ya-tenemos-un-acuerdo-con-el/ |access-date=March 24, 2022 |website=ElNuevoDia.com |language=Spanish}} joining them after South Bay's season ended. Tremont made his debut on April 11, 2022, powered Carolina's offense throughout the season, averaged 17.8 points and 8.0 assists 1.7 steals per game. He was selected as BSN Rookie Of The Year 2022 and leading in assists.{{Cite web |last=Tremont |first=Waters |title=BSN stats |url=https://www.bsnpr.com/jugadores/jugador?id=13375&e=10}} Waters joined the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web |title=Memphis Grizzlies 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612763/grizzlies |access-date=July 5, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} On July 26, 2023, Waters helped the Gigantes to win their first BSN title against the defending champions [[Vaqueros de Bayamón]]. They dominated the Vaqueros in five games.Carolina logra su primer campeonato en la historia del BSN. (n.d.-a). bsnpr.com. https://www.bsnpr.com/noticias/carolina-logra-su-primer-campeonato-en-la-historia-del-bsn ===Metropolitans 92 (2022–2023)=== On July 23, 2022, Waters signed with [[Metropolitans 92]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].{{Cite web |title=Le meneur de jeu Tremont Waters rejoint les Metropolitans 92 ! |url=https://www.metropolitans92.com/fr/actualites/2022-07-23/le-meneur-de-jeu-tremont-waters-rejoint-les-metropolitans-92 |access-date=July 23, 2022 |website=Metropolitans 92}} ===Return to Carolina (2024)=== On May 24, 2024, Waters signed with the [[Gigantes de Carolina (men's basketball)|Gigantes de Carolina]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].{{cite tweet|author=La Guerra del BSN|title=#BSNPR {{¡}} 💦 TREMONT WATERS AL CALENTÓN El armador Tremont Waters llega a Puerto Rico para reportarse a los Gigantes de Carolina y debutar mañana frente a los Capitanes de Arecibo. Waters viene de promediar 20 PPJ y 6 APJ en la CBA de China.|number=1794095865184899536|user=LaGuerraBSN|date=May 24, 2024|access-date=May 26, 2024|language=Spanish}} ===Shanghai Sharks (2024)=== On September 10, 2024, Waters signed with the [[Shanghai Sharks]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA).{{cite web |title=Sharks add Waters to their roster, ex Carolina |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/890952/Sharks-add-Waters-to-their-roster,-ex-Carolina |website=Eurobasket.com |access-date=3 October 2024 |date=10 September 2024}}{{cite web |title=Former Celtics player Tremont Waters signed with Chinese team Shanghai Sharks for the 2024-25 season. |url=https://hoopshype.com/rumor/3153183/ |website=HoopsHype |access-date=3 October 2024 |date=10 September 2024}} ===ASVEL Lyon-Villeurbanne (2026–present)=== On August 23, 2026, Waters signed with [[ASVEL Basket|ASVEL Lyon-Villeurbanne]] of the French [[LNB Élite]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web|title=Tremont Waters seals move to ASVEL|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/tremont-waters-seals-move-to-asvel/|date=August 23, 2026|website=euroleaguebasketball.net|access-date=August 23, 2026}} ==National team career== Tremont Waters is of Puerto Rican descent. He opted to play for the [[Puerto Rico men's national basketball team]] for the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.nhregister.com/colleges/article/Tremont-Waters-looking-to-earn-spot-on-Team-11353716.php|title=Tremont Waters looking to earn spot on Team Puerto Rico}} He was part of the team that helped Puerto Rico qualify for the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2024 Summer Olympics]] after defeating both [[Mexico men's national basketball team|Mexico]] in the semifinals and [[Lithuania men's national basketball team|Lithuania]] in the final of one of four [[2024 FIBA Men's Olympic Qualifying Tournaments]].{{cite web |title=Puerto Rico ends 20-year Olympic drought with historic win over
